name: Eating disorder recovery

image.caption: Troy Roness, Ed. M. (C/S): Unbroken: Mapping the Path to an Eating Disorder Recovery

lead: Eating disorder recovery is the process of getting better from conditions such as anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa and binge eating disorder. It means a return to regular eating and quitting restrictive habits, with physical and psychological recovery and a healthier body and body image.

Researchers say there are almost as many definitions of recovery as studies, with a trend toward including physical, behavioural and psychological components. In looksmaxxing forums, recovery posts appear alongside discussion of leanness and diet, where some members describe returning to regular eating as part of a wider personal reset. Wikipedia reports about 70% of people with anorexia nervosa and 50% with bulimia recover within five years.

paras: Treatment varies by disorder and can include counselling, dietary guidance, reducing excessive exercise and food avoidance, medication for associated symptoms, and hospitalisation in serious cases. Research highlights social support, social identity and perfectionism as factors. It is typically delivered by a clinical team.

Both anorexia and bulimia increase the risk of death, and only about 10% of people with eating disorders receive treatment. Anyone affected is generally directed to medical and mental health professionals.

angle.text: Recovery is discussed in looksmaxxing and diet communities as a return to regular eating and leaving restrictive habits behind, for a healthier body and body image. Researchers note there is no single agreed definition, spanning physical, behavioural and psychological change.

lead: Eating disorder recovery is the process of improving from an eating disorder. Researchers note that conceptually it should include physical, behavioural and psychological components, but this has not been applied consistently across studies [1][2]. A review described a long-standing problem that there are almost as many definitions of recovery as studies, with a general shift towards counting psychological and cognitive symptoms [2].

Treatment varies by disorder and may include counselling, dietary guidance, reducing excessive exercise and food-avoidance behaviours, medication for associated symptoms and hospitalisation in severe cases [3]. According to Wikipedia, about 70% of people with anorexia nervosa and about 50% with bulimia recover within five years, binge eating disorder recovery is estimated at 20% to 60%, and only about 10% of people with eating disorders receive treatment [3].
The topic appears in looksmaxxing communities, where leanness and diet are common subjects and some members post about recovering their eating.
infobox: Recovery from anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder and related conditions
Counselling, dietary guidance, medication for symptoms, hospitalisation if severe

paras: A study guided by theory identified a 'fully recovered' group using body mass index, absence of eating disorder behaviours and a psychological questionnaire, and compared them with partially recovered groups on psychosocial functioning and comorbidity [1]. A systematic review and qualitative meta-analysis found that recovered individuals emphasise criteria related to positive functioning, with no clear consensus on which additional criteria are most fundamental [4].

Studies of recovered individuals examine social support [5] and social identity, including the role of group identification in recovery [6]. Research has also looked at perfectionism across stages of recovery [7]. A study of people with lived experience described effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and UK lockdown on eating disorder recovery [8].

Studies are largely observational and qualitative, covering how recovery is defined and measured [1][2][4], social support [5], perfectionism [7] and social identity [6]. This overview does not summarise randomised treatment trials.

Some looksmax.org members post about recovery, for example one user describing a move from very low calorie intake back to eating again, alongside quitting substances and starting to exercise, and receiving congratulations from other members [9].

lore.intro: Recovery is not a core looksmaxxing topic, but members sometimes describe it as part of a personal reset [9].
